messages:
liz: Quick spike update: i played with a tiny overlay scheme for safetensors shards. think of it as 'mini-patchflow' 
- base shard immutable, overlay blobs contain per-layer small diffs (deltas) and an index.
liz: Goal: avoid full shard reuploads for small fixes (quant tweak, bias patch), speed rollbacks, and reduce egress when streaming.
mike: Curious about warmup interplay. if loader streams base + overlay, do we apply patches before kvcache fill or after?
tara: must apply before kvcache insert. otherwise cache will have mixed-version tensors. simplest: loader stages overlay into a transient mapping, then do kvcache hydrate from the staged view.
mike: staging implies extra memory. for large models that could blow memory when many workers start. need heuristic: only allow overlays < X MB or < Y% of model for in-place apply.
liz: agreed. manifest should carry overlay_size and an apply_cost_estimate (pages touched). loader can reject overlay if budget exceeded.
devsec: security note: overlays must be signed. manifest should include overlay_ids + signature. also support per-overlay KMS envelope when model is private.
ops-bot: deploy-note: created dev-s3/mini-patchflow namespace, buckets versioning=on, sample overlays uploaded.
mike: atomicity question: how to avoid half-applied state while serving? single-process pointer swap is easy (map A -> map B). cross-process? harder.
tara: controller-driven rehydrate model: update manifest with new overlay_id, notify workers, workers rehydrate and swap local mapping under safe barrier. we can use lease+grace period to drain in-flight requests.
liz: addition: kvcache entries tagged with (base_ver, overlay_id) tuple. lookup requires exact match. on manifest change we invalidate keys where overlay_id differs. cheap to implement.
mike: sounds good. what about streaming prefetch ordering? if overlay patches early bytes that streaming prefetch reads, we need to interleave reads from base and overlay seamlessly.
liz: index contains layer->byte-range map. loader requests byte ranges from base and overlay accordingly. overlay chunks are small and content-addressed so can be fetched in parallel.
tara: manifest verbosity: avoid per-byte maps. prefer per-layer ranges + small bloom for quick negative checks for layers untouched.
devsec: also add overlay_policy: allowlist signers, max_overlay_age, and audit_url. audits should surface overlay author and signed hash.
liz: perf tradeoff: applying deltas can cause memcpy/page faults. so overlay format should be chunked and page-aligned to reduce copy cost when mmaping.
mike: fallback behavior? if overlay fails checksum or apply, loader should treat manifest as inconsistent and fall back to a compatible pinned model variant. log and metric.
ops-bot: telemetry hooks: emit overlay_apply_latency, overlay_mem_delta, overlay_reject_reasons.
tara: rollout plan: spike -> dev canary, exercise small overlays only. then staged rollout for warm models with ephemeral workers. measure prefetch_oom rate.
devsec: one more: compaction. if overlays accumulate, provide a compact-roots job that materializes a new base shard incorporating overlays, then update manifest to point to new base and retire overlays. that keeps read path simple long-term.
liz: writing short RFC draft tonight: API sketches for WeightsSource.open_shard(uri, overlays=[]) and manifest schema (base_id, base_checksum, overlays:[{id,size,apply_map}], signature, compaction_hint). will add diagrams and kvcache version tag.
mike: thanks. also include an opt-in flag for "apply-in-prefetch" vs "apply-on-demand" so ops can tune memory vs latency.
liz: will do. TL;DR: mini-patchflow = small signed overlay blobs applied at load-time with manifest-driven staging, kvcache versioning, per-layer index, and a compaction job to avoid overlay sprawl.
